applicant_utility.summary: This is UM's flagship full award for non-EU/EEA master's applicants: 18 scholarships a year covering tuition, a EUR 1,550 monthly stipend for 13 or 25 months, visa costs, EUR 700 of insurance and a guaranteed room. The hard gates are the 10 December 2026 Studielink cut-off, a GPA of at least 7.5/10, age 35 on 1 September 2027 and no previous Dutch degree study. With only about 2% of applicants winning, the motivation letter, financial-needs statement and reference letter are what separate shortlist candidates, and you must be ready to accept both the allocated room and the two-week Pre-Academic Training starting the first week of August 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-performing non-EU/EEA applicants under 35 with a GPA of 7.5/10 or higher who need tuition and living costs covered and will commit to ambassador duties.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your target master's is on the published 2027-2028 participating-programmes list before applying
Submit the complete Studielink application file, and any handling fee, before 10 December 2026
Ask your referee early: the letter must follow UM's guidelines, be dated no earlier than February 2026 and be uploaded by you, not the referee
Prepare a transcript plus a grade-system explainer demonstrating the 7.5/10 (75%, or 3/4) equivalence
Draft the motivation letter on UM's template and the personal statement of financial needs
Diarise the 22-26 October portal outage and submit before 1 February 2027 23:59 CET
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 10 December 2026 master's application deadline, which disqualifies even outstanding candidates
Submitting incomplete files that cannot be corrected, since documents cannot be added or replaced after the single submission
A reference letter that ignores UM's guidelines, predates February 2026, or lists only a personal email for the referee
A GPA below the 7.5/10 equivalent without a convincing grade-system explanation
Assuming the room can be declined later: refusing the allocated accommodation cancels the scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Air tickets to the Netherlands, the approx. EUR 75 cleaning fee payable to Maastricht Housing, any programme handling fee, and second-year housing for two-year students once the room allocation ends.

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Studielink admission first to obtain the student ID, then one login to the UM scholarship form, all documents uploaded in a single submission before 1 February 2027; faculty ranking and an online interview precede the April 2027 decisions.

applicant_utility.summary: The UTS is a one-off EUR 3,000-22,000 cash award for top-decile non-EU/EEA students admitted to a UT master's, and UT pays no tuition on your behalf, so you must be able to fund the rest yourself. You need (conditional) admission before you can even apply, the form runs from 15 October 2026 to 1 April 2027 16:00 CET, and Academic IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in speaking is a hard gate. Two-year students can earn a matching second-year award by holding a 7/10 average and 50% of credits at the end of the third quartile of year one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EU/EEA applicants with a conditional UT admission who can cover tuition and living costs themselves and want an additional merit top-up.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for the UT master's first and chase the (conditional) admission letter, which can take up to 8 weeks
Have the UT student number ready before the form opens on 15 October 2026, 09:00 CET
Book the Academic IELTS early: 6.5 overall with 6.0 in speaking is mandatory
Confirm the programme is qualifying (not ITC, not the pre-Master track) and that the non-statutory tuition fee applies to you
Budget against UT's published cost-of-living and tuition-fee pages, since no bills are paid for you
Submit before 1 April 2027 16:00 CET; results are announced in the first week of May 2027
common_rejection_risks: Applying before the admission decision and student number exist, which makes the file impossible to submit
Being a UT graduate, a current UT student, or an EU/EEA national, all of which are explicit exclusions
Choosing an ITC programme or the pre-Master track, including pre-Master students continuing into a master's
Losing the award by later becoming eligible for the statutory tuition fee - UT requires immediate reporting and then cancels the scholarship
Treating the award as full funding when UT explicitly warns applicants who cannot cover the remaining costs not to apply
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees, housing, insurance and all living expenses - UT points to its own cost-of-living and tuition-fee pages and expects recipients to cover these from their own funds.

alerts: Only one UT scholarship can be awarded per student, so the UTS application is also the gateway to the Kipaji Scholarship

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Master's application and admission first, then the separate online UTS form with the UT student number between 15 October 2026 and 1 April 2027 16:00 CET; results follow in the first week of May 2027.
